To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The conducted noise of the buck converter is mainly due to the dV/dt of the switches and to the stray capacitances of the board.
The conducted common mode noise of the buck converter is mainly due to the drain to source voltage of the switches.
The conducted noise of the converter is dominated by the dV/dt noise from the switches drain to the source.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a noise modeling tool to predict the noise properties of a buck converter mounted on a PCB, and to identify the noise sources that can be controlled to reduce the impact of the noise in the powered system.
the characterization of noise properties of DC to DC converters for powering of sLHC detectors.
understanding the noise properties of a DC-DC converter and the noise couplings with the front-end electronics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
• The conducted noise from the converter to the ground plane is dominated by the dV/dt of the switches drain tracks, that develop common-mode currents on the input cable.
the conducted noise is well controlled and that the measured noise level is compatible with the requirements of the front-end system.

the conducted noise is well controlled by the LISN, and that the LISN impedance is the most important factor to be considered when designing the grounding, shielding and filter of the power converter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method to identify the noise sources of a DC/DC converter and we have characterized the noise properties of a prototype converter in a well defined test bench.
the conducted noise of the converter is well predicted with a simple model.
the PSpice model is able to reproduce the measured input and output current with a reasonable accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a well defined test environment is required to characterize and to model the conducted noise of a power converter.
the noise properties of a buck converter can be characterized in a controlled environment and that a model can be used to predict the common mode noise at the input and output of the converter.
the noise sources of a buck converter can be identified and controlled with a model based on a test setup and a measurement method that is reproducible.
